subject: Novomed: audit log inventory, export options, and delivery SLA
messages:
From: Jill Harper <jill.harper@novomed.com>

Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novomed: audit log inventory & export SLA request

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this — Novomed's security team is working through SIG/SOC2 evidence and we need a clear inventory of Redwood's admin/audit logging and the options for extracting that data (formats, integrity guarantees, delivery SLA). Specifically we need:

- A concise list of admin/privileged events you log (examples: role changes, key rotations, operator actions, model deployments, config changes).
- The fields included per event (timestamps, actor id/type, IP, request_id, payload hash, etc.).
- Retention policy (default and any tiers for privileged events).
- Export options (on-demand NDJSON/CSV, attested tarball, S3 presigned, SFTP), and expected delivery times for each.
- Chain-of-custody/integrity approach (signed manifests, checksums, HMAC).
- Any sampling/aggregation behavior that could omit or compress events.

We attached our evidence request (Novomed_Audit_Request_v1.pdf) for reference. If you can send a representative sample package (manifest + 24-48 hour slice) and an outline of SLAs, that would help us decide whether we need an attested package for our auditor.

Can we schedule a short 30-minute call next week to go over the sample and any redaction options?

Thanks,
Jill Harper
Director, Information Security
Novomed

Hi all — following up with technical details we will include in the inventory and the sample package. I included brief answers inline against Mina's bullets to keep context.

> - A concise list of admin/privileged events you log

We log (not exhaustive):
- Operator authentication events (login success/fail, token creation, session termination)
- Privileged config changes (route changes, quotas, SLO overrides)
- Model lifecycle events (deploy, rollback, pin/version changes)
- RBAC/permission changes (role grants/revokes, group membership)
- Key and secret operations (KMS/HSM key creation, rotation, deletion requests)
- Operator CLI/API actions (manual interventions, manual KV cache invalidation)
- Billing/usage overrides and SLA exception flags
- Data export requests (who requested, what slice, delivery method)

Each event record contains (schema summary):
- event_timestamp (RFC3339)
- event_type (string)
- actor_id, actor_type (user/service/operator)
- actor_role (if applicable)
- target_id, target_type
- request_id (uuid)
- request_payload_hash (sha256 of payload when applicable)
- session_id / kv_cache_id (if present)
- source_ip, geo_region
- user_agent
- outcome (success/failure)
- correlation_ids (trace/span ids)

> - Retention policy (default and tiers)

Default retention: 13 months for standard admin events. Privileged actions / signed audit records: 24 months (configurable for enterprise commitments). We can support legal hold/export snapshots beyond retention windows on an ad-hoc basis; that requires a signed request from your legal team.

> - Export options and SLA

Export formats: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) gzipped, CSV manifest (summary + checksums), optional Parquet for analytics. Delivery methods:
- On-demand slice via presigned S3 URL (we upload to a short-life bucket and provide URL): target delivery SLA 48 hours.
- Push to your SFTP endpoint (SSH key exchange preflight): 48-72 hours depending on queue.
- Attested forensic package (tar.gz) with signed manifest and notarized checksum: up to 5 business days.
- For automated recurring exports we can set up a cross-account S3 replication with agreed IAM role (requires 7-10 business days to provision).

Integrity & chain-of-custody:
- Package includes sample_manifest.csv (fields: filename, record_count, sha256, start_ts, end_ts).
- We will sign the manifest with Redwood's release key and provide an HMAC-SHA256 over the archived tarball.
- We keep an export audit trail (who requested, who approved, delivery URL, expiration) stored for 24 months.

Sampling/aggregation: we do not sample admin events by default. Long-term retention can include compression/aggregation for cost reasons; the raw event records for the retention window are available for exports unless you opt into archival compression.

Attachments in the sample package: sample_admin_events.ndjson.gz (24-hour slice), sample_manifest.csv. I will place the sample in a staging bucket and share a presigned link once Mina/Laura sign off.

Schema references: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-operator-event-schema (contains redwood:operator_event_v2 schema).

If Novomed needs redaction guidance, we can provide a sanitized pipeline (PII redaction rules) before packaging.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer — Runtime & Exports
Redwood Inference
